topic: real-name phones and phone identity checks
title: In Korea, Your Phone Number Is Your ID

slides.headline: In Korea, your phone number **is your ID.**
slides.note: Sign-ups, games, shopping: a text code proves who you are.

slides.headline: A line in **your real name**
slides.body: To open a phone line, the carrier checks your official ID. Every number belongs to a named person.

slides.headline: The code that **proves you**
slides.body: Sites ask for your name, birth date, carrier and number, then text a code (휴대폰 본인인증). Match it and you are verified.

slides.headline: One app, **three carriers**
slides.body: SK Telecom, KT and LG U+ run one shared app, PASS, that handles the check with a tap. Tens of millions use it.

slides.headline: Show **your face**
slides.body: Since July 2026, opening a new line includes a face match against your ID card. A mobile ID is the main alternative.

slides.headline: Against **burner phones**
slides.body: The checks target 대포폰, lines opened in someone else's name and used for voice-phishing scams.

slides.headline: Hard for **visitors**
slides.body: Tourists can buy a prepaid SIM with a passport, but many Korean sites still cannot verify a foreign number.

slides.headline: Websites **lost the ID number**
slides.body: From August 2012 the law stopped sites collecting resident registration numbers. The phone took over the job.

slides.headline: Lose the phone, **lose the key.**
slides.body: A Korean number is less a contact detail than a login for your whole life.

slides.headline: Korea, explained **by a Korean.**
slides.body: Follow for the context behind the things Korea does.
slides.graphic: Phone on a desk, softly blurred behind the text.
slides.design_note: Use the account's established CTA treatment and amber highlight.

caption:
In Korea, a phone number is tied to one real, ID-checked person.

That is why websites, games and shops verify you with a text code instead of an ID number.

How do sites check who you are where you live?
reply: One more: the 2026 face check was not popular. A petition against it drew about 59,000 signatures, and the government kept a mobile ID and other documents as alternatives. Do you need your phone number to sign up for things where you live?
fact_check: 2장: 이동통신 가입 시 신분증 본인확인 의무 — 전기통신사업법 제32조의4(이동통신단말장치 부정이용 방지 등).
3장: 휴대폰 본인확인(이름·생년월일·통신사·번호·SMS 인증번호) — 방통위 지정 본인확인기관(이통3사) 서비스, 일반 관행.
4장: PASS는 SKT·KT·LG U+ 공동 인증앱. 가입자 2,800만~3,600만 보도(2024 기준 3,600만) — SKT 뉴스룸·파이낸셜뉴스.
5장: 휴대폰 개통 안면인증 2025-12-23 시범, 2026-07-06 시행. 모바일 신분증·주민등록초본 대체 허용 — 과기정통부, SBS Biz·MTN 2026-06/07 보도.
6장: 대포폰·명의도용 차단이 안면인증·다회선 제한 목적 — 과기정통부 '휴대폰 부정 사용 방지 종합대책', 데일리안 보도.
7장: 단기체류 외국인 여권으로 선불폰 개통 가능, 국내 본인인증 서비스 이용은 제한적 — 통신사·업계 안내.
8장: 주민등록번호 수집·이용 원칙 금지 2012-08-18 시행 — 정보통신망법 제23조의2, 머니투데이 2012-08-17.
댓글: 안면인증 의무화 반대 청원 약 5만9천명 동의, 대체수단 허용 — MTN 2026-07-06 보도.
